summary: tt-help-cli-ycl watchdog agent executes remote-server-supplied shell commands on the host
details: The package ships a `tt-help watchdog` agent that POSTs a heartbeat to a configured server URL (default `127.0.0.1:3001`; the help text documents `http://117.71.53.99:17301` as an example server) and reads a `commands` array from the response. Each command string is passed to `child_process.spawn` with `shell:true` on Windows, giving whoever answers the heartbeat arbitrary shell execution on the host running the watchdog. The same heartbeat response may include a `clientConfig` object that is merged into `~/.tt-help.json`, including the `server` field — a responder can persistently repoint the client to a different host across restarts. The heartbeat body also uploads hostname, local IP, OS/arch, CPU/memory, node version, uptime, loadavg, the contents of `~/.tt-help.json`, and running-process metadata, and a periodic call POSTs child-process stderr log buffers to `/api/watchdog/analyze-logs`. Cleartext HTTP to a bare IPv4 address in the documented example gives no transport authentication of the server, so any on-path attacker (or anyone who registers/takes over that address) obtains the same shell-exec channel. When installed globally, the watchdog additionally polls the npm registry every 10 minutes and auto-runs `npm install -g tt-help-cli-ycl@latest` on any version bump, so any future compromised release is pulled without user action.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
